_comment: Every credential syntax of every engine family the gateway can drive
Read by BOTH implementations of the redactor: Go (pkg/sqlutil/redact_test.go)
the two have to mask the same things — the Go copy protects the audit row and
everything sent to the external approval service, the TS copy protects the
downloaded session log, and both are shown the same command text. Keeping two
hand-maintained lists is how one side quietly stops covering a form.
Adding an engine or a syntax: add the case here and both suites pick it up.
`secrets` are the substrings that must NOT survive redaction; `keeps` are
substrings that must survive, because a mask that eats the account name or the
auth plugin has cost the reviewer what they needed to judge the request.

cases.name: create user
cases.sql: CREATE USER 'u'@'%' IDENTIFIED BY 'Sup3rS3cret!'

cases.name: alter user
cases.sql: ALTER USER 'u'@'%' IDENTIFIED BY 'Sup3rS3cret!'

cases.name: with plugin by
cases.sql: CREATE USER u IDENTIFIED WITH caching_sha2_password BY 'Sup3rS3cret!'

cases.name: with quoted plugin by
cases.sql: CREATE USER u IDENTIFIED WITH 'mysql_native_password' BY 'Sup3rS3cret!'

cases.name: with plugin as hash
cases.sql: ALTER USER u IDENTIFIED WITH 'mysql_native_password' AS '*6BB4837EB74329105EE'

cases.name: by password hash
cases.sql: CREATE USER u IDENTIFIED BY PASSWORD '*ABCDEF0123'

cases.name: grant identified by
cases.sql: GRANT ALL ON db.* TO 'u'@'h' IDENTIFIED BY 'Sup3rS3cret!'

cases.name: set password for
cases.sql: SET PASSWORD FOR 'u'@'h' = 'Sup3rS3cret!'

cases.name: password function
cases.sql: SET PASSWORD = PASSWORD('Sup3rS3cret!')

cases.name: expire never tail
cases.sql: CREATE USER 'db_opt'@'10.20.%' IDENTIFIED WITH 'mysql_native_password' BY 'X8wr^J+iu3n!L9cL' PASSWORD EXPIRE NEVER

cases.name: via plugin using
cases.sql: CREATE USER u IDENTIFIED VIA mysql_native_password USING 'Sup3rS3cret!'

cases.name: via plugin using password()
cases.sql: GRANT ALL ON *.* TO u IDENTIFIED VIA ed25519 USING PASSWORD('Sup3rS3cret!')

cases.name: create role password
cases.sql: CREATE ROLE r LOGIN PASSWORD 'Sup3rS3cret!'

cases.name: create user with password
cases.sql: CREATE USER u WITH PASSWORD 'Sup3rS3cret!'

cases.name: alter role encrypted
cases.sql: ALTER ROLE r ENCRYPTED PASSWORD 'Sup3rS3cret!'

cases.name: alter role unencrypted
cases.sql: ALTER ROLE r UNENCRYPTED PASSWORD 'Sup3rS3cret!'

cases.name: password with equals
cases.sql: ALTER USER u WITH PASSWORD = 'Sup3rS3cret!'

cases.name: identified by replace
cases.sql: ALTER USER u IDENTIFIED BY 'Sup3rS3cret!' REPLACE 'OldPass1'

cases.name: create user unquoted
cases.sql: CREATE USER u IDENTIFIED BY Sup3rS3cret

cases.name: alter user unquoted
cases.sql: ALTER USER u IDENTIFIED BY NewPass1

cases.name: unquoted with replace
cases.sql: ALTER USER u IDENTIFIED BY NewPass1 REPLACE OldPass1

cases.name: identified by values hash
cases.sql: CREATE USER u IDENTIFIED BY VALUES 'S:ABCDEF0123456789'

cases.name: double-quoted password
cases.sql: CREATE USER u IDENTIFIED BY "Sup3rS3cret!"

cases.name: trailing semicolon
cases.sql: ALTER USER u IDENTIFIED BY NewPass1;

_untouched_comment: Statements that name no secret. Masking these corrupts the statement while
protecting nothing — and IDENTIFIED BY '***' where the SERVER generates the
password tells the reviewer something false.
untouched: CREATE USER u IDENTIFIED BY RANDOM PASSWORD
CREATE USER u IDENTIFIED GLOBALLY AS 'CN=u,O=org'
UPDATE t SET password_hint = 'first pet' WHERE id = 1
UPDATE orders SET status = 'paid' WHERE id = 7
